text.p: Italian bonds and Btp futures closed firmer after four consecutive lower sessions, consolidating gains along with other European debt markets after higher than expected German July jobless data which market took as a sign an interest rate hike was less likely.

The September Liffe Btp contract broke through first resistance at 135.35 and continued rising. The next barrier was seen at 135.85 and then at 136.30. "From a technical point of view today's correction was on the cards," a chartist said.
But operators noted that the positive session did not lessen worries about the dollar's continuing strength, although the greenback turn below 1.88 marks after an early 1.89 high.
In cash bonds, the July 2007 Btp gained 60 basis points to 101.30, yielding 6.67 percent and with the Btp/Bund spread at 101 bps after gapping out to 106 in early trade.
The May 15 2002 Btp closed 30 bps up at 100.06 while the May 15 2000 Btp ended 20 bps up at 99.79.
Dealers said there was some renewed moderate interest for short term Btps in the afternoon after being neglected in the morning.
The market is now looking for impetus from the U.S. where the 10-year T-bond auction takes place on Thursday.
